# Serena Ng — Product Designer

> Product designer working on patient experience and AI workflows at Epic Systems. Previously designed for Ronik Design Agency, Snyk, JFK Airport, and Reuters. BFA in UX Design from Northeastern University.

This site was redesigned in 2026. The full plain-text profile is at https://serenang.com/ (visible without JavaScript).

## Case studies
- [SearchNEU](https://serenang.com/searchneu/): Mobile redesign of a course search engine for Northeastern students.
- [JFK Airport](https://serenang.com/jfk/): Streamlining visitor escort requests for JFK Terminal 4.
- [Reuters x Ecolab](https://serenang.com/ecolab/): Interactive microsite promoting water sustainability in industry.
- [The Pomodoro Timer](https://serenang.com/pomodoro/): A productivity tool for the Apple Watch.

## Résumé
Product designer experienced in healthcare, cybersecurity, and enterprise tools. Designs with AI in the loop to prototype faster and close the gap between design and engineering.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ng-serena

### Experience
**Epic Systems — User Experience Quality Manager, Software R&D** (2025 – 2026)
- Removed MyChart Bedside's #1 adoption barrier by prompt-engineering an AI agent to auto-map configurations, and designing a human-in-the-loop confirmation workflow so analysts could trust its output, increasing adoption 30%
- Built a validation framework to QA the AI agent across 1,000+ real and edge-case scenarios, reaching a 97% AI mapping success rate
- Designed a MyChart lab result time estimate feature and prototyped it with Anthropic Claude, giving patients visibility into their visit
- Created a 0→1 Trauma Score calculator that turns a time-critical scoring protocol into a live workflow pre-populated with vitals and chart data
- Caught a color-accessibility gap that kept clinicians from distinguishing patient acuity, owned the safety escalation, and shipped a fix in 3 days
- Shadowed clinicians through full 12-hour shifts in NYC, Oklahoma, and Texas, running contextual interviews and usability tests on live workflows

**Ronik Design Agency — UX Designer** (2024)
- 1 of 3 designers at a design agency, owning projects end-to-end as sole or lead designer for 10+ clients including Reuters, Ogilvy, Ecolab, and PGIM
- Created a 0→1 security dashboard (desktop & mobile) for JFK Airport T4, replacing an email-based process for 7K+ monthly security vetting requests
- Built a 50+ component Figma design system to scale the JFK dashboard
- Redesigned login and signup for NBCUniversal Together, a B2B advertiser portal, making key actions easier to find and cutting user error 70%
- Designed and built a responsive infographic microsite (desktop & mobile) for Reuters and Ecolab with 30+ data visualizations and 15+ animated elements
- Presented multiple design directions per project and iterated through 15+ client feedback cycles, often on same-day turnarounds

**Snyk Cybersecurity — Product Designer and Researcher** (2023)
- Created 10+ workflows and 30+ screens for the flagship developer security platform, used by 2M+ users, and added 15+ components to the design system
- Designed Snyk's first SBOM import/export system, shaped by 10+ customer calls and usability tests amid rising government compliance requirements
- Proposed and led design of Snyk's first persistent notification center, scaling beyond one-off toasts to support ongoing async processes
- Led AI-assisted churn and renewal research across 5+ products and 3 years of data, presenting insights to 200+ stakeholders

**SearchNEU — Product Designer (Part-time)** (2022 – 2025)
- Owned the full mobile redesign of a course search platform with 7,000+ monthly active users, rebuilding 30+ components for mobile constraints while staying consistent with desktop
- Extended course-opening alerts from desktop to mobile, letting students track high-demand classes and reaching 25,000+ notifications sent per month

### How this portfolio was built
Serena designed this portfolio in Figma, then built it with Anthropic's Claude — working iteratively in conversation to turn the designs into a live, responsive site — and deployed it herself through GitHub Pages on a custom domain.

- Figma to live site in 7 days
- Optimized for humans and AI
- Dark mode shipped in 1 day
- AI-assisted motion design
- Built as a single-page React app, with every page, interaction, and animation directed by Serena and implemented with Claude
- Fully responsive, with dedicated mobile patterns: a bottom section nav with scroll progress, floating back buttons, and swipe gestures in galleries and book flippers
- Dark mode that follows the visitor's device setting, with a manual toggle and a radial transition that expands from the toggle
- Interactive details including a hover-to-reveal project preview panel, an animated journey timeline, a flippable book viewer, a fun-fact bubble, and a full-screen gallery slideshow
- Performance work for slow connections: compressed images and videos, lazy loading, and fade-in on load
- Made readable by AI tools and search engines: plain-text versions of every page, structured profile data, a sitemap, and an llms.txt summary
- Old portfolio URLs automatically redirect to their new pages, with a custom 404 page listing current links
- Deployed with GitHub Pages on a custom domain, with Google Analytics and Search Console set up
